name: Foziscribe
tagline: An AI scribe that turns spoken audio into cleaned up transcripts and structured notes.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The core of any AI scribe is now commodity: an audio file goes into a speech model, the text goes into a language model with a formatting prompt, and structured notes come out. A coding agent can wire that up locally in an afternoon with faster-whisper and a template prompt, and for solo use on recorded audio it will hold up fine. The gaps are the unglamorous parts: live streaming transcription with low latency, speaker labels that are actually correct, a phone app that survives a pocket, and pushing finished notes into whatever system of record you actually live in. Public detail on this particular product is thin, so treat the verdict as a judgment on the category rather than on a feature list. If the paid version is doing domain-specific templating or operating in a regulated setting, the DIY build is a hobby version of a serious tool.
coreLoopDIY: Drop in an audio file or record from the browser, get a timestamped transcript and an LLM-formatted note you can edit and export.
requirements: A machine that can run a Whisper-class model, or an API key for a hosted speech model
An LLM API key for the note formatting step
Patience for diarization, which is the part that will disappoint you
whatYouLose: Real-time transcription during a live conversation instead of after the fact
Speaker separation that is accurate enough to trust without reading the whole thing
A mobile app and reliable background recording
Handoff into other tools: shared docs, CRMs, EHRs, ticketing
Anyone to blame or call when a recording is silently lost
moatNotes: Scribe products mostly compete on latency, vocabulary accuracy in a specific domain, and where the finished note lands. None of those are model access.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the demo is easy and the last mile is not. Getting a transcript is free; getting a note that is correct on jargon, attributes the right line to the right person, arrives seconds after the conversation ends, and lands in the right place without copy paste is a product, not a script. Add any setting with a confidentiality obligation and the calculus changes again: people pay for a vendor agreement and an audit trail as much as the transcription.
notes: Post-hoc transcription is a solved weekend project; live and in-domain is still the paid part.
prompt:
Build a local AI scribe web app in an empty folder. Stack: Python 3.11, FastAPI, SQLite via sqlite3 (no ORM), server-rendered Jinja2 templates, vanilla JS, no build step, no frontend framework.

Features, in scope:
1. A single-page UI at / with two ways to add audio: a file upload (mp3, m4a, wav, mp4) and a browser recorder using MediaRecorder that posts the blob to the same endpoint.
2. On upload, normalize audio to 16kHz mono wav with ffmpeg via subprocess, then transcribe with faster-whisper (model size from WHISPER_MODEL in .env, default "small", CPU int8 by default).
3. Store recordings and transcripts in SQLite: id, created_at, title, source_filename, duration_seconds, transcript_json (segments with start, end, text), transcript_text, note_markdown, template_name, status.
4. Transcription runs in a FastAPI BackgroundTasks job. The UI polls /api/jobs/{id} every 2 seconds and shows status: queued, transcribing, drafting, done, failed. Failures store the error string and show it.
5. After transcription, send the transcript plus a chosen template prompt to an LLM via the OpenAI-compatible endpoint configured in .env (OPENAI_API_KEY, OPENAI_BASE_URL, MODEL). Ship three templates as editable markdown files in templates_notes/: meeting.md, interview.md, generic-summary.md. Each template is a system prompt plus an output skeleton.
6. A detail page per recording: left column is the transcript with clickable timestamps that seek an audio player, right column is the generated note in a textarea that saves on blur. Buttons: regenerate note with a different template, copy note, download note as .md, download transcript as .txt and .srt.
7. A list page of all recordings with title, date, duration, template used, and delete.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, login, multi-tenancy, teams, telemetry, analytics, payment, cloud storage, real-time streaming transcription, and speaker diarization. If speakers matter, just let the user type names into the note.

Rules: all secrets and model config in .env, read with python-dotenv, and ship a .env.example. Audio files live in ./data/audio, the database in ./data/scribe.db, both gitignored. Everything runs offline except the note-drafting call; if OPENAI_API_KEY is missing, skip drafting and still show the transcript.

Deliver: requirements.txt, app.py (or a small app/ package if it exceeds 400 lines), templates, static assets, and a README with exact setup steps including the ffmpeg install line for macOS and Debian. Then run the server and self-check by transcribing a short generated test wav.
